Community Guidelines

Last updated: 17 November 2026

Relay is for talking with friends. These rules keep it safe and friendly. Breaking them can get content removed or an account restricted, suspended or deleted.

Be respectful

  • No harassment, bullying, threats or hate based on who someone is.
  • Don't keep contacting someone who has blocked you or declined your friend request.
  • Don't impersonate other people.

Keep it legal and safe

  • Never share sexual content involving anyone under 18. We report it to the authorities.
  • No intimate images of anyone without their consent.
  • No content that promotes terrorism, violence, self-harm or illegal activity.
  • Don't share other people's private information (addresses, IDs, documents).

No spam or abuse of Relay

  • No spam, scams, phishing or malware.
  • No automated accounts, scraping or attempts to break Relay's security.

Reporting and blocking

If something's wrong, report the message or the person (press and hold a message, or open someone's profile → Report). The report keeps a copy of the reported text, so deleting it later doesn't hide it. You can also block anyone: they can't message, call or find you anymore.

If you or someone else is in danger, contact your local emergency services first.

What happens after a report

An admin reviews it and can remove content, warn, restrict (read-only for a while), suspend for a set time, or delete the account. Every action is logged. If you think a decision about your account was wrong, contact us: github.com/Anas2103/Relay/issues.
